title: 'March of the Jaguars': See Images From Netflix's First Latin American Nature Documentary
summary: The new film from Lawrence Wahba will premiere at the 50th edition of the São Paulo International Film Festival.
body_markdown:
On Saturday the 3rd, Netflix released the first images from


March of the Jaguars


, a new film from


Lawrence Wahba.


The feature film, created and produced in Brazil, is the first Latin American nature documentary on Netflix. It will premiere on


October 16


at the 50th edition of the São Paulo International Film Festival. The documentary is narrated by Oscar-nominated actress


Fernanda Torres


, as one of the jaguars. The film traces the journey of a clan of spotted jaguars. At the center is Patrícia, the matriarch of the clan (voiced by Fernanda Torres), who tells the story of her grandchildren, Marcela and Rio, as they grow from cubs to adults in an increasingly dangerous world. “When Mike Bueno and I began to follow a jaguar family in 2021, we couldn't even begin to imagine what lay in front of us. Slowly, moving at its own pace, nature revealed an extraordinary story, with charismatic personalities, drama, tragedy, danger, love, and resilience. A truly cinematic tale,” says director Lawrence Wahba. Over the course of five years, the team spent a total of 46 weeks — across 26 separate expeditions — in and around Encontro das Águas State Park, in the Pantanal of Mato Grosso state in Brazil. They worked with locals, known as "Pantaneiros," researchers, and park rangers to capture the world of jaguars as never before, Co-produced by Duo2 and Bonne Pioche,


March of the Jaguars


will premiere later this year on Netflix.

About Netflix:


Netflix is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time.


About Duo2


Duo2 is an independent Brazilian production agency that combines technology with entertainment to produce high-quality content across multiple formats and platforms. They have produced more than 400 hours of TV shows and documentaries, as well as corporate communication videos and independent projects. Co-produced with Brazilian channels such as TV Brasil, ARTE, MTV, Red Bull, Multishow, VH1, History Channel, A&E and Nat Geo, with projects appearing in more than 30 countries.


About Bonne Pioche


Bonne Pioche is an independent production agency founded in 1993. Bonne Pioche has produced 500 hours of documentaries, 20 feature films, 50 theater cast recordings, 3000 musical tracks, and a catalog of 600 hours for distribution. Among many other prizes, they received the Best Documentary Feature Oscar for the documentary "March of the Penguins." Bonne Pioche is currently run by two of its founders and producers, Yves Darondeau and Emmanuel Priou.
